title: O the Delights, the Heavenly Joys
description: O the Delights, the Heavenly Joys in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 17 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 91, headed “The glory of Christ in heaven”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O the de-lights, the heav-enly joys, The glo-ries of the place Where Je-sus sheds the bright-est beams Of his o'er-flow-ing grace.

lines: O the delights, the heavenly joys,
Where Jesus sheds the brightest beams
And all the glorious ranks above
To see him wear the crown.
And lay their highest honours down
Those soft, those blessed feet of his
High on a throne of light they stand,
His head, the dear majestic head
This is the Man, th' exalted Man,
But when our eyes behold his face,
Our hearts shall love him more.
Lord, how our souls are all on fire
Our tongues rejoice in tunes of praise
And whilst our faith enjoys this sight,
We long to leave our clay,
And wish thy fiery chariots, Lord,
Shout to the Lord, and let our joys
Ye British skies, resound the noise
Thee, mighty God, our souls admire,
And join with the celestial choir
Thy power the whole creation rules,
Sits smiling at the weak designs
Thy scorn derides their feeble rage,
Flings vast confusion on their plots,
Their secret fires in caverns lay,
But gloomy caverns strove in vain
Their dark designs were all reveal'd,
Praise to the God that broke the snare
In vain the busy sons of hell
Their souls shall pine with envious rage,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
